newsitem.title: UK: ROYAL CARIBBEAN TO GAIN OSLO LISTING.
newsitem.headline: ROYAL CARIBBEAN TO GAIN OSLO LISTING.

text.p: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd said that it intended to go ahead with a secondary share listing on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
The Miami-based cruise shipping firm said the listing reflected the global nature of its business and the firm's links with Scandinavia.
The Oslo Stock Exchange said its board had approved the application from Royal Caribbean.
"Since we are a completely global operation, and some of our major shareholders are based in Scandinavia, we felt it was appropriate to apply for this secondary listing," a company spokesman said.
No new shares will be issued as part of the secondary listing, he added. Royal Caribbean shares will trade under the code RCL.
Royal Caribbean recently completed the acquisition of Celebrity Cruise Lines Inc, making it a rival to cruise industry leader Carnival Corp.
Oslo has emerged as a leading stock market for shipping, cruise and offshore firms.
Royal Caribbean will be the third cruise shipping firm listed. NCL Holding is already quoted, while Miami-based Cruise Holding Ltd has announced plans for its own listing.
"With three cruise ship companies listed, the Oslo Stock Exchange will command a leading position as the international equity market for cruise shares," the Oslo exchange said.
Oslo's Stock Exchange Board also approved listings for two other firms.

Nordic American Tanker Shipping Ltd will have a secondary listing on the main list, and Bergen-based Tordenskjold Shipping ASA will gain a listing on the SMB list for small and medium-size businesses.
